evidence.field: 說文解字 / 說文解字注
evidence.text: The entry gives two received Shuowen forms: “助也。从口从又” and “手口相助也。从又从口.” The commentary discusses differing component order and says the received explanation is problematic. This is evidence for the textual tradition and its internal variation, not direct proof of the graph's original formation.
evidence.title: 右 yòu - 汉典

evidence.field: 字形 / 訓義 / 聲系
evidence.text: This account analyzes 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, and interprets 右 as ritual service followed by assistance. It rejects the Shuowen/Duan hand-and-mouth explanation as the graph's original construction. It says oracle-bone forms used 又 for divine assistance and cites assistance uses in bronze inscriptions. This is a distinct scholarly interpretation; it does not demonstrate that 口 was merely a meaningless distinguishing mark.
evidence.title: 右(ウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.text: The entry lists an oracle-bone example as 鐵7.4 合20836 and early Western Zhou bronze examples including 右作旅鼎, 小盂鼎, 班簋, 夨令方彝 and 師旂鼎, followed by Chu slips, Shuowen seal, Qin slips and clerical forms. This establishes catalogued graphic witnesses across script traditions, but the page does not date the oracle-bone specimen or independently establish the transition sequence.
evidence.title: 右 yòu - 汉典

evidence.field: OC / MC / gloss (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, character row 又)
evidence.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 row for 又 gives Mandarin yòu, Middle Chinese hjuwH, Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s, gloss “also, in addition.” These are the exact local row readings; the locally supplied 右 rows give *[ɢ]ʷəʔ (MC hjuwX, “right hand”) and *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s (~ *m-qʷəʔ) (MC hjuwH, “right hand”). The shapes are comparable in this system, but the table readings alone do not prove either a sound-component role or a whole-graph loan. The upstream PDF could not be opened during this invocation.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Kotobank, 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.text: The entry dates Japanese usages separately: 右方 in a contest is cited from 898; directional 右 from 栄花物語, dated circa 1028–1092; and documentary “above/previously stated” 右 from a late-eighth-century 万葉集 note. These are Japanese textual examples, not evidence for the ancient Chinese graph's first sense or graphic history.

evidence.text: The entry catalogs senses including assistance, blessing/protection, right hand and side, west, rank and urging food (通侑). It cites classical works for these uses, but those citations are not independently dated here as first attestations, nor do they establish a chronological semantic chain among direction, ritual service, blessing and assistance.

gaps: No primary paleographic record directly examined here settles whether 右 began as 又 denoting the right hand and gained 口 as a graphic differentiator, or whether 口 was meaningful in a ritual-prayer compound. The two accounts remain disputed; the claim that 口 is necessarily meaningless is unverified.

The catalog entries name inscription collections and bronzes, but no dated original inscription image and context were inspected. A precise first attestation and earliest sense cannot be assigned from these sources.

Semantic chronology is unresolved: dictionary citations separately record directional, assistance, blessing/protection, rank and banquet-related uses, but they do not establish when the senses arose or their semantic links.
The Shuowen commentary discusses differing textual versions and component order, but no critical manuscript or primary textual witness was examined to resolve possible corruption.

Local 又 and 右 Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were supplied and checked as local data. The official Unihan pages and Baxter–Sagart PDF were not externally verified as opened pages; no external evidence item here treats those exact local readings as externally authenticated.

A source about right-hand form and oral prayer indicates a proposed semantic construction for the whole graph, not proof that 又 functions as a phonetic component. No independently verified evidence in this search establishes a phonetic component analysis.
No reusable-source bulk terms were verified; a tracked extract is not recommended.
